confirmed: Source version is arXiv:2412.18940v2, dated 14 February 2025, with the stated title and authors; the PDF has 28 pages and includes Appendices A-C (PDF p. 1, arXiv stamp and author block; pp. 24-28, Appendices A-C).

S1 is a supervised remote crossover, appropriately coded lab_rct: songwriting was conducted over Zoom with shared screens, and both task prompts and system conditions were randomized across sessions (PDF pp. 11-12, Section 7.2).
S1 compares Assist (Amuse plus Aria) with Baseline (Aria alone); both conditions provide generative AI, and each participant completes both (PDF pp. 11-12, Section 7.2).

S1 analyzes the same 10 people in both conditions, comprising eight hobbyists and two professionals; condition counts must not be added, and fewer than 50 people were analyzed (PDF p. 11, Section 7.1 and Table 3; p. 14, Figure 8; p. 16, Figure 10).
The paper reports 10 recruited songwriters but no separate count at randomization; leaving S1 n_randomized null avoids claiming an unreported assignment count (PDF pp. 11-12, Sections 7.1-7.2).

Each songwriting task requested an 8-bar chorus of chords and melodies, with 25 minutes allowed per session within a 2-hour study; the prompts concern an unexpected friendship and a favorite summer holiday memory (PDF pp. 11-12, Sections 7.1-7.2 and Figure 6).
The Amuse implementation uses gpt-4o-2024-05-13, while the comparison retains Aria; the stated model version is supported (PDF p. 7, Section 4.4; p. 11, Section 7.2).

S1 creativity and quality measures are post-task self-reports on a seven-point agreement scale, analyzed with Wilcoxon signed-rank tests; neither questionnaires, interviews, nor interaction logs provide an eligible creativity/diversity score on participant-produced output (PDF p. 12, Section 7.3; pp. 17-18, Section 8.3 and Figure 11; p. 26, Appendix C.1).
Expressiveness reported string matches exactly: Assist=6.00±0.63, Baseline=4.20±1.66, z=4.00, p=0.028; the paper itself labels the statistic z (PDF p. 17, Section 8.3.2).

Exploration reported string matches exactly: Assist=6.10±0.83, Baseline=4.40±1.50, z=3.00, p=0.019; this is perceived exploration, not a count of produced ideas (PDF p. 17, Section 8.3.2; p. 26, Appendix C.1).
Musical Coherence reported string matches exactly: Assist=6.00±1.18, Baseline=6.00±0.89, z=10.50, p=1.00; this is the songwriter's own assessment (PDF p. 18, Section 8.3.4; p. 26, Appendix C.1).

The one-line finding correctly reproduces the expressiveness contrast, identical musical-coherence means, and their p-values, while explicitly identifying them as self-reports (PDF p. 17, Section 8.3.2; p. 18, Section 8.3.4).
S2 comprises eight hobbyists in 1-hour semi-structured formative interviews; it is not an assigned creative-output experiment (PDF p. 3, Section 3.1).

S3 compares model prompting methods, each evaluated over 100 sets of 30 four-bar chord progressions; these are generated outputs rather than people, and Self-BLEU measures variation within generated sets (PDF p. 9, Section 6.1; p. 10, Table 1).

S4 uses 25,000 LSTM Prior progressions, 25,000 GPT-4o progressions, and 3,242 Amuse progressions against a reference corpus of 25,601 progressions; these are model/corpus units, not participant counts (PDF p. 10, Table 2 and Section 6.2.1).

S5 has 45 analyzed Prolific listeners after four of 49 recruits failed attention checks; 900 denotes judgments across the two listening tasks, not people. Listeners compare generated clips and do not produce AI-assisted creative work (PDF p. 10, Section 6.2.2 and footnote 2).

Appendix B.3 evaluates the same synthetic audio used in the listening study with CLAP; it does not score the songwriters' compositions. The remaining appendices contain prompts, implementation details, survey/interview questions, and thematic codebooks as stated (PDF pp. 24-28, Appendices A-C and Tables 4-6).

Core exclusion and context_class=none are supported: S1 meets the random-order criterion but fails the analyzed-people threshold and output-scoring criterion; other components are interviews or technical evaluations, and the paper is not a synthesis (PDF p. 3, Section 3; pp. 9-12, Sections 6-7; pp. 17-18, Section 8.3; p. 26, Appendix C.1).
summary: The 10-songwriter randomized crossover reports self-rated creativity and quality, so it does not meet the requested definition of a randomized study with creativity or diversity scored on participants' outputs. Reported numbers and eligibility conclusions are supported, but company involvement, the code URL, and the listener-exclusion field need correction.
